steps.body: When two lines cross, they make four angles. Angles **across** from each other are **vertical angles** — always **equal**. Angles **next to** each other are **adjacent** — they share a side and add to 180° along each line.

steps.body: At a crossing, you get everything from one angle. If one angle is 75°: across is 75° (vertical, equal); next to it is 180 − 75 = 105° (adjacent on a line); across from that is 105° again.
steps.narration: At a crossing, you get everything from one angle. If one angle is 75°: across is 75° (vertical, equal); next to it is 180 − 75 = 105° (adjacent on a line); across from that is 105° again.

explanationVariants: Adjacent angles at a crossing fill a straight line: 180 − 75 = 105°.

numericErrors.feedback: That's the vertical angle (across) — the next-door angle fills the line: 180 − 75 = 105.

widget.prompt: Two lines cross and one angle measures 40°. Find all four angles.

authoredStages.title: Across
authoredStages.body: The vertical angle across from 40° is also 40° — vertical angles are equal.

authoredStages.title: Next door
authoredStages.body: Each adjacent angle fills a straight line with 40°: 180 − 40 = 140°.

authoredStages.title: The full set
authoredStages.body: So the four angles are 40°, 140°, 40°, 140° — and 40 + 140 + 40 + 140 = 360°, a full turn.

widget.successFeedback: Exactly — one angle unlocks all four, and they always total 360°.

steps.body: Crossing lines make equal vertical pairs across, and 180° adjacent pairs along each line.
takeaways: Vertical angles (across the crossing) are equal.
Adjacent angles at a crossing add to 180°.
One known angle unlocks all four (they total 360°).
